title: On Namsan
description:
The cable car lifted slowly. Below, the whole city sank away.
Daeun pressed her forehead to the glass and looked down. "Minjun, over there... you can see our neighborhood." Somewhere in the direction her fingertip traced, the convenience store where she pulled all those nights would be, too.
Seoul looking that small — Daeun was seeing it for the first time. The city she walked every day fit entirely inside one span of glass.

The giant Namsan tonkatsu came out the size of a face. With a practiced motion, Daeun cut hers in half and moved it onto {name}'s plate. "Things like this taste better shared." Sharing out her own portion was second nature to her.

They went up to the observation deck. Beyond the wall of glass, Seoul's night stretched on without end — and across the river, one place burned brighter, clustered close. Gangnam.
The goal he'd chased for five years, and for the first time he was looking down at it standing beside her. Those lights that felt close enough to touch if he reached for the glass.

Among all those countless lights, where {name}'s eyes finally settled was—

choices.text: Across the river, the lights of Gangnam.
choices.result_text:
From up here, it really did look close enough to grab. Put a hand to the glass, and those lights sat in his palm.
Which made it feel farther. A distance that's almost-but-not-quite within reach wears at a person more than one that's simply far.
The distance of a single pane of glass felt vast tonight. Daeun was right beside him, and for a moment he forgot even that.

choices.text: Daeun's profile, watching the view.
choices.result_text:
More than the view, it was Daeun's profile watching the view that caught his eye. The lights drew the line of her face soft.
"...What are you looking at, not the view?" Feeling the look, Daeun turned and smiled. The tips of her ears were a little red, but she didn't hide it.
The view would be here tomorrow, and next year too. But this profile was here today, beside {name}. That felt more certain, somehow, than Gangnam.

choices.text: The dark side where the lights don't reach.
choices.result_text:
Among all the brilliant lights, there was a dark corner the light didn't reach. Out at the edge where the city's glow ran out — the direction of the hometown.
He glanced beside him, and Daeun was looking at the same place. Not the bright side, but the dark one.
Neither of them said a word. That each of them was looking at their own hometown, at what they'd left behind, in that darkness — they knew without saying it.

choices.text: My own face reflected in the glass.
choices.result_text:
Over the night view, {name}'s own face was overlaid in the glass, half-transparent. The lights of Gangnam passed straight through it.
The day he reaches those lights — will this face do. Standing there, just as he is now, could he do it without shame.
{name} looked, a long moment, at that face in the glass. The answer didn't come easily.

title: The Lock
description:
Along the deck railing, padlocks hung packed together. On each colored lock, someone's name and date. Daeun stood in front of them.
She fiddled with one lock between her fingers, then, carefully, spoke.
"Should we... hang one too?" Her face knew it was childish. And still, without hiding it, she asked, plainly. Her eyes shone a little.

choices.text: Hang it — childish or not, lock today in place.
choices.result_text:
They bought a small lock and wrote their two names side by side. Fastened it to the railing, and Daeun flung the key down hard into the dark below. That it couldn't be undone now — that, somehow, felt good.
"Come find it in ten years, us." Daeun smiled. How they'd find it with no key, they both laughed knowing.
One of the thousands of locks on that railing was, now, the two of theirs. Strangely, that felt like something solid. That somewhere in the city, their today was locked away.

choices.text: Don't — we don't need this kind of thing.
choices.result_text:
"We don't need this kind of thing, right?" When {name} smiled, Daeun smiled along with him.
"...That's very you too, Minjun." She might well have been let down, but there was no letdown in her voice. If anything, she turned the words over as if she liked them.
Even without locking today into a single padlock, the two of them already knew each other. The walk down without a lock was, strangely, light and good.

title: On Namsan
description:
"It's close enough to just walk up, honestly." Jiyeon said it, and yet the cable car tickets were already bought, in her own hand, first. Her words and her hands running separate was an old grammar of hers.
The whole way up she didn't look out the window. The city shrinking below wasn't a new sight to her. A life of looking down from high places — she'd already lived it.

The giant Namsan tonkatsu. "This is that famous?" she asked, unimpressed, and cleared the face-sized plate without leaving a bite. The reason it was famous, her mouth admitted and her words did not.

The observation deck. Beyond the wall of glass, across the river, the lights of Gangnam burned in a cluster.
"Oppa's goal — from here, it's right over there." Jiyeon pointed with her chin. To her, the lights of a familiar neighborhood. To {name}, lights he still hadn't reached in five years. Over the same lights, the distance between the two of them was that different.

Among all those countless lights, where {name}'s eyes finally settled was—

choices.text: Across the river, the lights of Gangnam.
choices.result_text:
From up here it looked close enough to grab. Which made it feel farther. That almost-but-not-quite distance was what had squeezed {name} for five straight years.
Jiyeon read that look from beside him. She knew exactly what oppa was thinking — she was someone who'd walked out from under her own father to have a world of her own.
She said nothing. Only, that silence had a different grain than her usual pride.

choices.text: Jiyeon's profile, watching the view.
choices.result_text:
"...What." Jiyeon turned, and this time she didn't play it cool — she just smiled.
Brighter than the night view, that smile.

choices.text: The dark side where the lights don't reach.
choices.result_text:
He looked at the place the lights didn't reach. "You came from somewhere like that." Jiyeon said it quietly.
There was no scorn in it. It was just a fact.

choices.text: My own face reflected in the glass.
choices.result_text:
Over the night view, my face was overlaid, half-transparent.
When I reach those lights, will this face do. {name} looked at himself in the glass a long time.

title: The Lock
description:
The railing was packed with padlocks. Jiyeon crossed her arms in front of them.

"...So people actually do this." She said it, but her feet didn't move.

choices.text: Hang it — childish or not, lock today in place.
choices.result_text:
"Childish." She said it, and threw the key. Then took out her phone and photographed the lock.
The one who called it childish kept a picture.

choices.text: Don't — we don't need this kind of thing.
choices.result_text:
"We don't need this kind of thing." Jiyeon turned first.
"Yeah, that's us." {name} followed her down, smiling.

title: Lost Child
description:
The amusement park. The parade started and a crowd surged.
In the middle of it, a child was crying. Before {name} could, Daeun knelt down.
"Did you lose your mom? I'll help you find her."

Helping find the parents took the whole afternoon. They'd only gotten on two rides.

choices.text: Stay with the child to the end, together.
choices.result_text:
They went all the way to the lost-child center. The mother bowed again and again, crying.

They'd only ridden two rides. But Daeun said this:
"We didn't get to ride much. ...But today was the most fun."
{name} knew, strangely, that it was true.

choices.text: Hand the child to staff and go back to the rides.
choices.result_text:
He handed the child to a staff member and turned away. It was the correct thing to do.
They rode everything, and Daeun smiled too.
But she brought up that child one more time, on the way home.

title: The Highest Point
description:
The amusement park. Jiyeon picked the very front row of the roller coaster like it was obvious.
Right before the peak, as the rail stood straight up into the sky, she grabbed {name}'s hand.
"Oppa, from up here even Gangnam looks small."

Coming down, churros in hand, they stood in front of the photo booth.

choices.text: Take the whole four-frame strip.
choices.result_text:
They took four frames in the booth. In the last one, Jiyeon suddenly kissed his cheek, so {name}'s face came out a mess.
"This one's yours." she said, and slipped the other strip into her own wallet.

choices.text: Skip the photos, ride it again.
choices.result_text:
"Photos, please." Jiyeon pulled {name} by the hand and got back in line.
Front row, again. At the peak, {name} saw her laughing without a sound.

title: Dawn Alley
description:
Dawn, after helping her close. The city had not woken yet. Before locking the door, Daeun took two cans of coffee from the warmer. Once the shutter was down, she handed one to {name}. Their fingertips met, leaving behind a warmth that did not belong to the can.

Only the convenience store sign washed the alley in thin yellow light. No delivery truck yet. No first bus. They stood before the shutter with both hands around their cans, their breath appearing between them and vanishing in the wind.

Fatigue sat beneath Daeun's eyes after the night shift. Tonight, she did not cover it with the first smile. She traced the rim of the can once, opened her mouth, then closed it again.

choices.text: Wait for whatever she was about to say.
choices.result_text:
{name} did not hurry her. Something clicked softly inside the can, then the alley went quiet again.

Daeun noticed the silence he was holding open for her. At last she let out a long breath and looked up at him without arranging her face first.

choices.text: "Rough night?" Ask first.
choices.result_text:
It was an ordinary question, but Daeun did not answer with an automatic I'm fine. She tightened both hands around the can and nodded.

"A little." After that, the words she had swallowed all night began to come out.

title: Someone Who Waits
description:
"Minjun, sometimes you wait too long for me."

Daeun said it without smiling first. It was not a complaint. It sounded like she still did not know what to do with someone who made room for her like that.

"Do you hate it?"
"No. That's why I end up saying more. I don't usually talk about this stuff."

She told him, briefly, about the customer who had worn her down and the bill that was overdue. When the last sentence ended and {name} was still there, some of the tension left her hands around the can.

choices.text: Answer by meeting her eyes.
choices.result_text:
"...Minjun."

Nothing followed his name. Daeun raised her chin a little. This time, {name} did not look away.

title: Allowed Not to Be Fine
description:
"It was a little rough."

Daeun did not brush it aside. At two in the morning, a drunk had knocked over a display. The owner wanted next week's shifts changed again. Her voice grew quieter as she spoke, but her eyes did not hide.

"It's strange. Around you, I feel like I'm allowed to say I had a hard night."
"That's not strange."
"Good."

Daeun looked down at the rim of the can, then back up. Relief and nerves occupied the same face.

choices.text: "You can tell me that anytime."
choices.result_text:
Daeun gave the smallest nod. "Then can I say one more thing now?"

Before he could ask what, she lifted her chin. Their eyes came to rest at the same height.

title: One Step
description:
When the words stopped, only the outdoor unit at the end of the alley and the sound of their breathing remained. As the steam above the cans thinned, the single step between them became more exact.

Daeun did not move away. Both hands still held the can, but the tension left her shoulders. She asked with her eyes first, and waited while {name} understood the question.

One beat. Two. Their breath rose between their faces and slowly came apart.

choices.text: In that silence, close the distance first.
choices.result_text:
{name} stepped half a pace closer. Daeun did not step back. Her fingers tightened around the can, and from this close he could see it happen. One beat. Two. Before the steam faded, the last of the distance was gone.

The kiss was brief and a little clumsy, warm against the cold dawn air. Even after they parted, neither of them moved. Daeun smiled first. Her eyes were wet, but she was not crying.

"We're really in trouble now, aren't we?" She called it trouble, but {name} had never seen her look so bright. The coffee had gone cold. Neither of them cared.

choices.text: Press the coffee into her hands — that's enough for tonight.
choices.result_text:
{name} let the impulse pass and pressed the cooling can firmly back into her hands. "You should go inside. It's cold."

Daeun remained where she was for a moment, looking almost as if she had expected something else. Then she smiled without trying to hide it.

"Minjun, you really are..." She did not seem to know whether the unfinished sentence held relief or disappointment. Not rushing made sense with him. If not tonight, there would be another chance. The certainty felt warmer than the dawn air.

title: In the Car
description:
Jiyeon pulled her black sedan into a side street in Gangnam and killed the engine. {name} stayed in the passenger seat, seat belt still fastened. Neither of them said anything about getting out.

The dashboard kept a low afterglow. When the heater stopped, Seoul's lights spread thinly across the windshield. Once the radio was gone, only their breathing and the cooling engine remained.

Jiyeon looked straight ahead for a long time. Anyone else would have gotten a line from her by now. Tonight she only pressed her lips together once. Her hand left the wheel, but did not return to the ignition button.

choices.text: Do not rush her. Watch the windshield with her.
choices.result_text:
{name} looked ahead too. Their reflections on the glass faded and returned with the changing traffic lights.

With someone beside her who did not break the silence, Jiyeon took a few measured breaths. Then she spoke first.

choices.text: "You're quiet tonight." Smile first.
choices.result_text:
One eyebrow lifted. Jiyeon looked caught for half a second, then her usual expression returned.

"I'm not allowed to be quiet?" She tried for cold. The end of the sentence did not quite make it.

title: Engine Off
description:
"Uncomfortable?"
"No."
"Then why are you sitting so still?"

{name} watched her profile reflected in the windshield. "Because being quiet together is fine."

Jiyeon's fingertips tapped the center console once and stopped. She could have laughed at the answer or brushed it aside. She did neither. Instead, she turned slowly toward him. The crack in her composure did not last long. This time, {name} was there to see it.

choices.text: Hold her gaze when she turns.
choices.result_text:
In the close cabin, not looking away felt a great deal like moving closer.

Jiyeon drew a breath. Her lips shifted as if she meant to get some line out first.

title: You Notice Everything
description:
"I'm not used to you being quiet."
"You notice everything."

The answer came quickly, but Jiyeon did not start the engine. Her finger rested at the edge of the button while light from the windshield crossed the back of her hand.

"So you hate it?"
"No. I like this side too."

The corner of her mouth moved as if she might scoff. She never quite managed it. Instead, she turned toward {name}.

choices.text: Do not cover it with a joke. Look at her.
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon's eyes reached his first. It was not the look she used when she meant to win.

With no words left between them, the distance inside the car became suddenly exact.

title: Half a Second
description:
Jiyeon turned all the way toward him. Between the driver's seat and the passenger seat, the center console that usually looked broad had narrowed to the width of one resting hand.

"...What are you looking at?"

A cool line, but the end of her voice wavered for half a second. Her eyes did not leave his. Only the fingers above the console flinched once. Before another sentence could cover the crack, there was a single beat left for either of them to choose.

choices.text: In that half-second, close the distance.
choices.result_text:
{name} did not let that half-second pass. In the narrow car, one beat was enough to close the distance. The kiss was brief. Jiyeon neither closed her eyes nor pulled away; her shoulders only tensed, then softened.

When they parted, she faced the windshield at once. "...Eyes front." Her voice had lost nearly all of its usual edge.

Jiyeon pressed the ignition button. Each passing streetlight caught the red at the tips of her ears. She pretended to see only the road ahead. No one spoke before the car began moving again — but the air had already changed completely.

choices.text: Just smile — "Nothing."
choices.result_text:
"Nothing." {name} smiled. Jiyeon shot him a look. "...You're no fun." She tried to toss it off, but she left the engine off, her hand hovering above the ignition button.

In the narrow car, they watched the lights blur across the windshield. Even without rushing, the silence did not feel wasted.

When Jiyeon finally pressed the button, she murmured, "...Next time, I won't let you off." Neither of them said what she had let him off for. Neither needed to.

title: That Child
description:
He was shopping at the mart when someone tugged his sleeve.
It was the child who'd been lost at the amusement park. Holding mom's hand, and not crying this time.

"That man! The man who found me!" The child waved.
The mother recognized him and came over to say hello.

choices.text: Greet them warmly.
choices.result_text:
"Thank you so much back then. He still talks about that day."
He waved it off as nothing, but a corner of his heart went warm.

A small kindness, coming back around like this — no interest charged.

title: Four Frames
description:
Catching a ride in Jiyeon's car, he flipped down the sun visor and something dropped out.
It was the four-frame photo strip from the amusement park. Down to that last frame where her face came out a mess.

The cool one had been keeping this tucked up here all this time.

description_if_known.arc_jiyeon_wedding_gap_seen:
He was opening the fridge when he stopped.
The four-frame amusement park strip was stuck there with a magnet. On the newlywed fridge.

Even after marrying, Jiyeon hadn't thrown it away. The things a cool person quietly keeps.
{name} looked at that strip a little longer.

choices.text: Pretend not to notice and put it back.
choices.result_text:
He put the strip back where it was. Said nothing to Jiyeon.
If he had, she'd have said something like "I meant to toss it and forgot," for sure.

Quietly keeping things wasn't only her way.
